\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آستین} (āstīn)}{آستین (āstīn)}]{\ur{آستین} (āstīn) — a sleeve}

\label{lesson:UR-C500-astin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to spin (thread), then the Urdu for a knot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آستین}}
\textbf{\ur{آستین}} — \emph{āstīn} — \textquotedblleft{}a sleeve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{قمیض} \ur{کی} \ur{آستین} \ur{لمبی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is qamīz kī āstīn lambī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sleeves of this shirt are long.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آستین}} (\emph{āstīn}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{āstīn}, \textquotedblleft{}a sleeve\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āstīn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āstīn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is qamīz kī āstīn lambī hai.} — The sleeves of this shirt are long.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to spin (thread), then the Urdu for a knot, then say \emph{āstīn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{آستین} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A sleeve\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سلوانا} (silvānā)}{سلوانا (silvānā)}]{\ur{سلوانا} (silvānā) — to have (clothes) sewn}

\label{lesson:UR-C500-silvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a knot, then the Urdu for a sleeve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سلوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{سلوانا}} — \emph{silvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have (clothes) sewn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{درزی} \ur{سے} \ur{نیا} \ur{کرتا} \ur{سلوایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne darzī se nayā kurtā silvāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I had a new kurta made by the tailor.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{نئی} \ur{شلوار} \ur{سلوائی}, \emph{us ne naī shalvār silvāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سلوانا}} (\emph{silvānā}) is the second causative of \emph{sīnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to sew\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{sīvyati}, \textquotedblleft{}sews\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13444): to have someone sew.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{silvānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{silvānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne darzī se nayā kurtā silvāyā.} — I had a new kurta made by the tailor.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a knot, then the Urdu for a sleeve, then say \emph{silvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سلوانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have (clothes) sewn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ادھیڑنا} (udheṛnā)}{ادھیڑنا (udheṛnā)}]{\ur{ادھیڑنا} (udheṛnā) — to unpick (stitches)}

\label{lesson:UR-C500-udherna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a sleeve, then the Urdu for to have (clothes) sewn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ادھیڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ادھیڑنا}} — \emph{udheṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to unpick (stitches)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{درزی} \ur{نے} \ur{پرانی} \ur{آستین} \ur{ادھیڑی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darzī ne purānī āstīn udheṛī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The tailor unpicked the old sleeve.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پرانا} \ur{کرتا} \ur{ادھیڑا}, \emph{us ne purānā kurtā udheṛā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ادھیڑنا}} (\emph{udheṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{udheṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to unravel\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{uddharati}, \textquotedblleft{}takes out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2009).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udheṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darzī ne purānī āstīn udheṛī.} — The tailor unpicked the old sleeve.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a sleeve, then the Urdu for to have (clothes) sewn, then say \emph{udheṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا} (rafū karnā)}{رفو کرنا (rafū karnā)}]{\ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا} (rafū karnā) — to darn}

\label{lesson:UR-C500-rafu-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to have (clothes) sewn, then the Urdu for to unpick (stitches).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{rafū karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to darn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{درزی} \ur{نے} \ur{میری} \ur{پتلون} \ur{رفو} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darzī ne merī patlūn rafū kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The tailor darned my trousers.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پرانا} \ur{کوٹ} \ur{رفو} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne purānā koṭ rafū kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{rafū karnā}) is built from \emph{rafū}, \textquotedblleft{}darning\textquotedblright{}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{rafw}, and \emph{karnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rafū karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rafū karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darzī ne merī patlūn rafū kī.} — The tailor darned my trousers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to have (clothes) sewn, then the Urdu for to unpick (stitches), then say \emph{rafū karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رفو} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To darn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ادھڑنا} (udhaṛnā)}{ادھڑنا (udhaṛnā)}]{\ur{ادھڑنا} (udhaṛnā) — to come unstitched}

\label{lesson:UR-C500-udharna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to unpick (stitches), then the Urdu for to darn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ادھڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ادھڑنا}} — \emph{udhaṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to come unstitched\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میری} \ur{آستین} \ur{ادھڑ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merī āstīn udhaṛ gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sleeve has come unstitched.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{جیب} \ur{ادھڑ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh jeb udhaṛ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ادھڑنا}} (\emph{udhaṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{udhaṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be taken out, to be unravelled\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{uddharati}, \textquotedblleft{}takes out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2009).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udhaṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merī āstīn udhaṛ gaī.} — My sleeve has come unstitched.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to unpick (stitches), then the Urdu for to darn, then say \emph{udhaṛnā} again
\end{itemize}
